punchline: Kindergarteners draw without a worry, adults forget how, and the book says the tools never left.
thirty_sec: Dan Roam found visual thinking when a last-minute presentation made him sketch a simple framework on a napkin, and it cleared his head. His claim is that any problem gets clearer with a picture, and that you need no artistic skill: your eyes, your mind's eye and your hand are enough. Kindergarteners draw freely, he notes, and adults have simply forgotten.
